newsitem.title: USA: Investor group seeks control of Raymond.
newsitem.headline: Investor group seeks control of Raymond.

text.p: A New York-based group of investment partnerships said Wednesday it has 7.51 percent of Raymond Corp. and has joined with other holders who have agreed to back its effort to take control of the board.

In a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, the group including Beford Falls Investors L.P. and Metropolitan Capital Advisors Inc., said it has urged Raymond Corp. management to sell or merge the company.
The group also said its agreements in which other holders have agreed to back its board nominees give it voting power of 2,572,484 shares, or 24.27 percent of the total.
The total includes 1,776,484 shares, or 16.76 percent, held by the other holders who include George Raymond, a company director, and members of his family, the group said.

The group said it sent the company's management a letter on Feb. 18 requesting a meeting to discuss its proposal for a sale or merger of Raymond Corp., a Greene, N.Y.-based maker of material handling systems.

It said it intends to propose "stockholder action" necessary to increase the size of the company's board to 13 from 10 and to elect its nominees to fill six current board vacancies. Those six nominees, along with Raymond, would give the alliance a majority of the votes on the board.

Raymond, a former chairman of the company, said last May that he was considering selling his stake in the company and that he had asked his fellow directors if they were interested in selling the company. He said they were not.

The Metropolitan Capital group, which includes its executive officers Jeffrey Schwartz and Karen Finerman, said it acquired its entire stake of 796,200 shares between Jan. 6 and Feb. 15 for about $14.91 million at prices ranging from $17.125 to $21.625 a share.
